extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funds (K-12 and higher education) including Title IX Coordinators and school administrators
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and regulatory requirements on the definition, offering, coordination, limits, and procedural handling of Title IX "supportive measures" for complainants and respondents, including Title IX Coordinator duties and related notification and delegation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title IX Coordinator duty to offer and coordinate supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (f)(1)(ii) requires a Title IX Coordinator to offer and coordinate supportive measures under §106.44(g), if appropriate, for a complainant upon being notified of conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination and to offer and coordinate supportive measures for a respondent if the recipient has initiated grievance procedures under §106.45 (and if applicable §106.46) or has offered the respondent an informal resolution process under §106.44(k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinator must proactively offer/support for complainants upon notification; respondents receive offers only when grievance procedures have been initiated or informal resolution offered. The Coordinator may delegate duties but retains ultimate oversight (see delegation criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification when complainant is unknown
rubrics_metrics.description: Under paragraph (f)(1)(iii)(A), when a complainant is unknown, the Title IX Coordinator is required to notify the individual who reported conduct that reasonably may constitute sex discrimination of the grievance procedures under §106.45 and, if applicable, §106.46, and the informal resolution process under §106.44(k), if available and appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures reporters (who are not identified complainants) receive information about available procedures and informal resolution options; notification should be provided when appropriate and available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to respondent upon complaint
rubrics_metrics.description: Under paragraph (f)(1)(iii)(B), a Title IX Coordinator must notify a respondent of grievance procedures under §106.45, and if applicable §106.46, and the informal resolution process under §106.44(k), if available and appropriate, if a complaint is made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respondent notice obligations trigger when a complaint is filed; ensures respondent is informed of procedures and options (but supportive measures to respondent are conditioned on initiation/offering of procedures).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initiation of informal resolution
rubrics_metrics.description: Paragraph (f)(1)(iv) requires a Title IX Coordinator to initiate a recipient's informal resolution process under §106.44(k) if available and appropriate and requested by all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informal resolution may only be initiated if it is available, appropriate for the matter, and all parties request it; Coordinator facilitates initiation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'supportive measures' — core elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures mean individualized measures offered as appropriate, as reasonably available, without unreasonably burdening a complainant or respondent, and not for punitive or disciplinary reasons; intended to restore or preserve equal access to education, protect safety, or provide support during grievance procedures or informal resolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition aligns with §106.44(g) and §106.2. Measures should be tailored, have the listed purposes, and not be imposed for discipline/punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures not mandatory in every case
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient is not required to provide supportive measures in every case; many supportive measures will not burden a party at all, and all supportive measures are subject to limits in §106.44(g)(2) and may be challenged under §106.44(g)(4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients have discretion but must adhere to the statutory/ regulatory limits (not punitive, not unreasonably burdensome).

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid implying preliminary findings in offering measures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department deleted language suggesting supportive measures should 'deter the respondent from engaging in sex-based harassment' to avoid implying a recipient should make a preliminary determination that a respondent engaged in sex-based harassment when considering supportive measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When offering measures, recipients should avoid wording or processes that suggest a preliminary finding of responsibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safety focus is on 'the parties' and educational environment
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department replaced 'temporary measures that burden a respondent that are designed to protect the safety of the complainant' with 'measures that are designed to protect the safety of the parties' and stated supportive measures may also protect the recipient's educational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Safety analyses should consider both parties and the educational environment; supportive measures cannot be justified solely as punitive actions against a respondent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures may be non-temporary and modifiable
rubrics_metrics.description: By removing 'temporary' from the definition, the Department acknowledges some supportive measures may not be temporary; recipients determine appropriate length of time. §§106.44(g)(3) and (4) permit modification or termination and provide parties the ability to seek modification or termination when a measure does not meet the definition or circumstances change materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should document duration rationale; parties may request changes or challenge measures under §106.44(g)(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment: supportive measures not for punitive or disciplinary reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.2 and §106.44(g)(2) state supportive measures must not be imposed 'for punitive or disciplinary reasons.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures that coincide with disciplinary sanctions at the conclusion of grievance procedures may be used as supportive measures earlier, but must not be imposed as punishment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures must not unreasonably burden either party
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department modified §106.44(g)(2) to clarify that supportive measures must not unreasonably burden a complainant or a respondent and must be designed to protect the safety of the parties or the recipient's educational environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must assess and avoid imposing unreasonable burdens; determinations are fact-specific and should be documented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology preserved as 'supportive measures'
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declined to replace the term 'supportive measures' with 'equitable interim measures,' explaining 'supportive measures' accurately reflects measures available even if a complainant does not move forward or after a complaint is dismissed and are not limited to the pendency of a grievance procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use 'supportive measures' in policies and communications to align with federal rulemaking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of 'party' meaning
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department added a definition to §106.2 clarifying that 'party' means a complainant or respondent and revised the definition of 'supportive measures' to reference 'a complainant or respondent'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and communications should use 'complainant' and 'respondent' rather than the more ambiguous 'party' in the supportive measures context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient ultimate responsibility and permissible delegation
rubrics_metrics.description: The recipient itself is responsible for compliance with Title IX, including duties assigned to the Title IX Coordinator; recipients may designate more than one Title IX Coordinator and delegate specific duties to designees, but one Coordinator must retain ultimate oversight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delegation is permitted to align with institutional structures, but the institution remains liable for meeting obligations under Title IX; documentation of delegation and oversight recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of confidential employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Confidential employees may provide counseling or services but are not required to offer and coordinate supportive measures because confidentiality may prevent them from coordinating across offices. Title IX obligations remain despite state laws that designate confidential employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should ensure confidential employees inform survivors how to contact the Title IX Coordinator; do not rely solely on confidential employees to meet coordination obligations required by Title IX.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures offered regardless of filing decision (complainants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures must be offered to complainants, as appropriate, regardless of whether grievance procedures are initiated (including when a complainant elects informal resolution or chooses not to initiate grievance procedures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer supportive measures whenever appropriate to restore/preserve access, even if no formal complaint is filed; document offers and refusals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures for respondents conditioned on notice/procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may be offered supportive measures, as appropriate, but only if grievance procedures have been initiated or an informal resolution process has been offered (because respondents will not always receive notice if complainant elects not to move forward).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not generally offer respondent supportive measures absent initiation/offering of procedures unless circumstances otherwise support an offer consistent with rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supportive measures available for all forms of sex discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to limit supportive measures to sex-based harassment; supportive measures are available for all forms of sex discrimination to restore or preserve access to the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should consider supportive measures across the full range of Title IX-covered sex discrimination.

rubrics_metrics.name: No mandate to publish additional supportive measures information
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department declines to require recipients to publish additional information about supportive measures, provide information in particular formats or languages, or work with Principal Designated School Officials, while noting recipients may choose to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions may proactively publish and translate supportive measures information, but are not required by this rule to do so; ensure any outreach complies with other regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Illustrative examples and recipient discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: Final §106.44(g)(1) provides illustrative examples of supportive measures (e.g., counseling, housing changes, academic adjustments) to assist recipients while leaving maximum flexibility to determine reasonably available measures limited by the requirement that measures restore/preserve access and not be punitive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples as guidance rather than an exhaustive list; recipients retain discretion but must justify measures consistent with definition and limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonably available standard
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department replaced 'available and reasonable' with 'reasonably available' in final §106.44(g)(1): supportive measures must be reasonably available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess availability against institutional resources and provide measures that are feasible; document inability to provide particular measures when claimed.

rubrics_metrics.name: No-contact orders: mutual and non-mutual allowed and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department modified the language to 'restrictions on contact applied to one or more parties,' clarifying that recipients may apply mutual or non-mutual no-contact orders as supportive measures, but such orders must not be imposed for punitive reasons and must not unreasonably burden a complainant or respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider factors such as party need, ages, nature of allegations, ongoing interactions (shared housing, classes, employment), and existing mitigation (civil protective orders). Recipients must ensure orders comport with First Amendment considerations and do not burden more speech than necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactive supportive measures permitted when appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures may include retroactive measures (e.g., retroactive withdrawals, extensions of deadlines, transcript adjustments, tuition reimbursements) that, if reasonably available, can be appropriate to restore or preserve a party's access to education.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should consider retroactive remedies for harms experienced prior to reporting, subject to reasonableness and availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Involuntary changes (class, work, housing) not categorically prohibited
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department eliminated 'voluntary or involuntary' language; supportive measures may include involuntary changes in class, work, housing, or assignments provided they are not imposed for punitive reasons and are not an unreasonable burden on a party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether an involuntary change is permissible is fact-specific; recipients must evaluate potential burdens and document rationale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary burdensome supportive measures (§106.44(g)(2)) — conditions and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures that impose burdens on a respondent may be permitted when necessary to protect a complainant's safety or access to education, provided they are not punitive or disciplinary and do not unreasonably burden a party; such measures are subject to §106.44(g)(2) limits and may be challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should ensure these measures are narrowly tailored, supported by a safety/risk analysis, documented, and accompanied by procedures for challenge/modification to address due process concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Challenge and modification process for supportive measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Supportive measures are subject to challenge under §106.44(g)(4); §§106.44(g)(3) and (4) permit modification or termination of supportive measures and provide parties with the ability to seek modification or termination when a measure does not meet the definition or circumstances change materially.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must maintain processes for parties to request modification/termination and must document decisions and any changed circumstances that justify modification or continuation.
